_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'English Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 10, Topics 10.1-10.5. Original topic/sub-topic names and Specific Outcome statements as documented in this file's prior version's own notes. Rebuilt 2026-08-31 to add real term/week/content data from a second real source, a complete 'SCHEME OF WORK' covering all 3 grades × all 3 terms, organized week-by-week and lesson-by-lesson (not by skill-strand block like the CDC syllabus's own structure) — the user explicitly chose a full rebuild around this source's real teaching units rather than a lighter overlay onto the old skill-strand topics, given how differently the two are organized. Real PII stripped, per standing sourcing policy: every term header in the source repeated a real individual's full name; removed and does not appear anywhere in this file. The source's own publisher/repackager branding (a materials-vendor name, not an individual's real school) was also removed from every header, out of caution. Topics here are the real 'Unit' themes this source actually teaches (e.g. 'Unit 1: Teachers and Teaching'), each containing the real individual lessons (Reading, Composition, Structure, Oral, Summary — genuinely interleaved within a unit in the real record, not grouped by strand); weeks with no named unit (mostly term-opening orientation weeks) are grouped under 'General Language Skills'. Each sub-topic's week_number is the real week it was first taught; where the source's own table cell for a lesson was just 'As above' (repeating the prior lesson's content across a second/third period in the same week), only the first occurrence is kept rather than duplicated. Content was extracted programmatically from the source's raw table (thousands of individual cells across 9 grade/term blocks) rather than transcribed by hand, then spot-checked for parsing errors before being written here; a handful of rows whose table formatting was too garbled to confidently attribute were left out rather than guessed.
